steps.intro: Before the pictures: the words from the lesson, all in one pattern. Read the Russian, say the whole line — It's gotten a lot greener — then tap to check.
steps.note: -er / -ier for short words and -y words · more for long, -ed and two-word adjectives · quieter / more quiet, livelier / more lively — both fine · good → better, bad → worse · a lot / much + -er, not “more busier” · less + the plain form: less green.

steps.instr: Six places, then and now: in each picture, the left half is the place before, the right half is the place now. Your turn first: look at the picture for a minute. What has changed? Say four sentences — It's gotten a lot … / It's become a lot more … — with the box beside you. Then tap to see which words fit, and check yourself in the next step.
steps.ans: **livelier · greener · cleaner · nicer · safer** (or: busier, more lively)
steps.note: Next step: one way to say it — compare it with what you said.

steps.intro: Now one way to say it. Say each missing word in the right form, then tap to check — and compare with what you said.

p: (lively) — there's a market now, and people sit outside at the cafés.
(green), too: there are trees and flower boxes everywhere.
(clean) — no more litter on the ground.

steps.note: lively → livelier (or: more lively) · -y → -ier · nice → nicer · safe → safer · a lot / much + -er, not “more cleaner”.

steps.instr: Your turn first: look at the picture for a minute. What has changed? Say four sentences — It's gotten a lot … / It's become a lot more … — with the box beside you. Then tap to see which words fit, and check yourself in the next step.
steps.ans: **emptier · quieter · more run-down · dirtier · less lively · worse**
steps.note: Next step: one way to say it — compare it with what you said.

steps.intro: Now one way to say it: the word in the right form, then tap to check.

p: (run-down): most of the shops have closed down, and the paint is peeling.
(dirty), too — there's litter all over the sidewalk.

steps.note: quiet → quieter (more quiet is possible, but less common) · run-down → more run-down · less + the plain form: less lively, not “less livelier” · bad → worse.

steps.instr: Your turn first: look at the picture for a minute. What has changed? Say four sentences — It's gotten a lot … / It's become a lot more … — with the box beside you. Then tap to see which words fit, and check yourself in the next step.
steps.sit: [A little brick house: before and now.]
steps.ans: **more built-up · busier · more crowded · more dangerous · noisier**
steps.note: Next step: one way to say it — compare it with what you said.

steps.intro: Now one way to say it — with less help: the whole comparative is hidden, the letters in brackets start the adjective. -er or more? Say it, then tap to check.

p: (b…-u…): there are apartment buildings all around the little house.
(d…) for people on foot — the cars pass really close.

steps.note: two-word adjectives (built-up, run-down) and -ed adjectives (crowded) → more · long adjectives: more dangerous · busy → busier.

steps.instr: Your turn first: look at the picture for a minute. What has changed? Say four sentences — It's gotten a lot … / It's become a lot more … — with the box beside you. Then tap to see which words fit, and check yourself in the next step.
steps.ans: **fancier · busier · more crowded · more touristy · noisier**
steps.note: Next step: one way to say it — compare it with what you said.

steps.intro: Now one way to say it: the letters start the adjective — -er or more?

p: (f…): there are hotels and restaurants all along the water.
(t…): tour boats, people with suitcases everywhere.
(n…) — you can hear the tour boats all day.

steps.note: fancy → fancier · noisy → noisier · but touristy (three syllables) → more touristy · touristy, not “touristic” (often a bit negative: full of things for tourists).

steps.instr: No help now. Choose three adjectives. For each one, say what you can see. Then tap the yellow box to see one way to say it.
steps.sit: [An old elevated highway in the city center — and the same place now.]
steps.ans: It's gotten **a lot greener**: there are trees and plants along the water. It's **much quieter**, too — there's no traffic. And it's **safer** for people walking and cycling.
steps.note: or: cleaner, nicer, more peaceful · a lot / much + -er · an elevated highway = эстакада (BrE: a flyover)
